And who were Krstic and Kusic who should have "finished all of it"? Krstic was the lieutenant-colonel who led the cleansing of Novoseoci in Sokolac in 1992. That was when he was a lieutenant-colonel, back when Eastern Bosnia was being cleansed. That was an operation in which the men were separated from the women and children, the women and children expelled, and the men executed. Here is Krstic's first report of that operation: "During the day the village of Novoseoci was ciscenje," cleansed or mopped up, "in Glasinacko Polje." And by 1995, Krstic was a general and during the course of the Srebrenica operation was appointed commander of the Drina Corps by Karadzic. Here's an intercept between Krstic and Zvornik Brigade Chief of Staff Dragan Obrenovic on the 2nd of August, 1995, reflecting Krstic's continuing efforts to cleanse Eastern Bosnia, efforts that continued since 1992 and on into 1995. "Krstic: Are you working down there? "Obrenovic: Of course we are working. "Krstic: Good. "Obrenovic: There are a few more who got caught. "Krstic: Uh-huh. "Obrenovic: Either by the gun barrel or mines. "Krstic: Kill them all, God damn it. "Obrenovic: Everything is going according to plan. "Krstic: Don't leave a single one alive. "Obrenovic: Yes? "Krstic: Don't leave a single one alive. "Obrenovic: Everything is going according to plan, everything." And Kusic, Kusic was a major political and military figure from Rogatica who was a member of the SDS Main Board, a man who led the cleansing of Rogatica in 1992. And in 1995, here's a report from Kusic reflecting how, just like Krstic, he was finishing the job in Srebrenica. "On the 7th of August, 1995, in the afternoon, in the canyon of the Praca river, five remaining balijas," that's a derogatory term for Bosnian Muslims, "who were after the fall of Zepa travelling along the following route ..." and he specifies that route in detail. "... went down to the railroad tracks at Dub and tried to reach Renovica, walking on the railroad tracks. They were liquidated. "The group was separate and it travelled for ten days. "The same day, in the vicinity of Luke, an unarmed Ustasha born in Srebrenica, 24 years old, was liquidated. Before he died he said that he fell behind the others and he was looking for food." In short, Your Honours, Radovan Karadzic, the supreme commander, was directly responsible for Directive 4 and Directive 7, both of which were aimed at driving all Muslims from Srebrenica; was anxious to get it going. Karadzic pushed Krstic to move the plan along faster. Once his forces began the attack, he specifically approved a shift in the immediate operational plans and sent his forces into Srebrenica. As soon as his forces took Srebrenica they immediately informed him. He was similarly informed that it was going according to plan, and that Muslims were being removed in great numbers in an operation that required coordination with many municipalities, and informed that Muslims were being captured in great numbers. Mladic told him as soon as the civilians were bussed out of Srebrenica that Srebrenica is done. Karadzic delivered in code an order to take Muslim prisoners from Bratunac to warehouses elsewhere. His hand-selected civilian commissioner told him that Muslim prisoners were being murdered or had been murdered at Kravica warehouse. He called the Main Staff headquarters when he heard that Muslim men were escaping to Muslim-held territory, the one aspect of the operation he regretted. And he covered up with the press the fact that the VRS had prisoners and that they were killing them. And he continues to say it didn't happen. Your Honours, the crimes in Srebrenica, the mass expulsion of the women and children, the mass killings of the men, these terrible facts have been proven time and again in other trials before this Tribunal. Now, we know there are some who out of nationalist fervour may stubbornly or naively claim that Srebrenica never happened. But when the man who was the supreme commander of the forces who committed the crimes, the man who acknowledged that he set those forces in motion, the man who was in contact with his forces throughout, when that man denies what happened, it is because he knows that the truth condemns him. But the living victims, the survivors, the women, elderly, those who were children in Potocari in July 1995, for them there is no question of what happened, only the lasting pain of loss. For those survivors, there's been no recovery, no restoration of lives that have not and cannot be restored as they were before their husbands, fathers, brothers were taken from them and murdered. Their ongoing tragedy, Your Honours, is part of the lasting legacy of the accused's crime and part of the overwhelming evidence that belies his efforts at denial. Your Honours, I will conclude shortly, but before I do I want to say a few more words about Karadzic's cover-up of crimes. For the cover-up of the organised killings and the wholesale expulsions in Srebrenica represent just another step in Karadzic's consistent pattern of hiding, deflecting, excusing, and denying, denials to internationals and the media about cleansings, denials to the internationals and media about crimes in the face of allegations and information from international negotiators, from UNPROFOR, from ICRC, from UNHCR, from the Special Rapporteur, from Security Council Resolutions, from the print media, from television, in the face of what was happening before the world, many of these allegations were explicit and anguished. Let me show you one, the second report in October 1992 of the Special Rapporteur for the UN and that followed his most recent mission in Bosnia. In his October 27th report he said, and I quote: "As indicated in the first report, the Muslim population are the principal victims and are virtually threatened with extermination." That's just a small snap-shot of the repeated condemnations, the repeated confrontations, the repeated allegations that were made to Karadzic. But as Karadzic quoted one of his commissioners as saying: "We are skinning the cat alive before the whole world." And as reflected in that quote, Karadzic didn't need the international community to tell him about the plight of the Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats within those Serb-claimed territories because apart from the allegations he was receiving, apart from the reports from the army and from the police, apart from the admissions and acknowledgements of -- from those within his circle that we've already heard -- at least some of which we've already heard, even a cursory look at the documents, the meetings, for example, at the Assembly sessions, reveal the awareness of the campaign against non-Serbs. Here, for example, is an -- a session of the Assembly at which an objection was posed to a proposed standard for citizenship in RS, that would be a standard based on birth, and that objection is revealing albeit unintentionally. "Second, the citizenship of Republika Srpska shall be acquired among other things by birth in the territory of Republika Srpska. This refers to all the Muslims and Croats we expelled. In reality, they are also citizens of Republika Srpska." All the Muslims and Croats we expelled. And, accordingly, the bill was sent back to the ministry for review upon Krajisnik's initiative. Or look at this comment in 1995 from a deputy at the Assembly: "Sometimes, Mr. President, one should not listen to the patriarch either. He is a holy man and we are practical men, practical men who want to make a state. A state is made by killing, slaughtering, imprisoning, and arresting people, every state in the world, including our own." Or perhaps this quote which puts it simply and perhaps wraps it up. This is from January 1993, again at the Assembly: "Believe me when I say that we cannot live together anymore. I don't know under what conditions we could live together now. I have to be honest and say that they caused so much evil to us" and this was -- that was a reference to World War II and the Ottoman occupation and the history, and continuing the quote, "and this time we did not cause less evil for them either." And over and over again Radovan Karadzic did his best to cover up this evil. Take the camps, for example. The Court has already seen some of the evidence about civilians in camps, including the report by Karadzic's own minister of the interior in mid-July to him that: "Crisis Staffs and War Presidencies have requested that the army round up or capture as many Muslim civilians as possible." But he couldn't let the world know this. Here, for example, is a letter to The Guardian at the end of July, 1992, 30 July 1992. This was sent by Karadzic to The Guardian. "Your article on the front page of today's newspaper is sensational. It is completely false to suggest that the Bosnian Serbs have organised concentration camps or that we hold civilian prisoners." The effort to mask the campaign against non-Serbs or to present it in some acceptable terms extended to the issuance of fig-leaf orders to follow international law. I referred earlier to one of those orders issued at the commencement of the attack on Srebrenica. In some instances, as you'll see, Your Honours, their interest, that is, the interest of these orders in international consumption, is rather clear on its face, as is the case of this signed order in August addressed to the General Staff and to the police in English that: "Forced transfer of people and other illegal measures against civilian population must be prevented." Or to take another example, you'll see a July 1992 telegram to the presidents of municipalities in the Gorazde area, a telegram that those municipality presidents were responsible for ensuring the protection of villages in which Croat and Muslim inhabitants hand over weapons and do not intend to fight. This at a time when the army and the police were engaged in cleansing villages. And interestingly, one municipality president had the nerve to write back directly to Karadzic and note that he wasn't the one who controlled the army and the police. But even beyond their occasionally transparent nature, such orders clearly have no meaning in the abstract, and when placed in the context of widely known massive crimes fulfilling Strategic Objectives, crimes that were not punished but, as you'll hear, were rewarded with promotions, their pretextual nature is unmistakable. Officers and commanders were not disciplined for cleansing Muslim or Croat villages; on the contrary, the accused promoted and rewarded and encouraged those responsible for crimes. On January 9th, 1994, for example, Karadzic held a ceremony announcing that: "Contrary to all the lies and slander of international propaganda-mongers, the Serbian army maintained the knightly character and military honour worthy of it," and bestowed awards on his military leaders including men like Radoslav Brdjanin, Vojo Kupresanin, Ratko Mladic, Dragomir Milosevic, Miroslav Deronjic, Stanislav Galic, as well as notorious units like Mauzer's Panther Brigade unit from Bijeljina. Karadzic's orders to investigate crimes were similarly cosmetic. It was not until ITN TV News broke the story of the horrors of the camps in early August, which set up days of intense and worldwide media coverage, that an investigation was ordered into this network of camps. You'll have a chance to see those investigations, but here, for example, is the investigation into the whole of the camps in SAO Krajina, a page and a half. The report on camps in the ARK was similarly feeble. Manjaca camp where 3500 people were detained warranted about or less than 300 words. Keraterm camp which had about 4.000 people go through it warranted less than 60 words. Not a word about crimes committed. Not a word about investigating those who committed crimes. There was also a report by the Ministry of the Interior, a report which relied upon, for example, Simo Drljaca, the local police chief who ran the Omarska camp. A report that was sent to a commission that included one of the investigators of the camp. Again not a word about crimes. And Drljaca, in conformity with the practice of rewarding and elevating ethnic cleansers, not only continued but was promoted and decorated. But the investigations, the denials served only to bolster his, Karadzic's, false claims to the international community that no cleansing was taking place. All these denials were part of keeping everything hidden. For just as General Mladic had said back in May of 1992, and he'd said this at the 16th Assembly session when he was selected as the Main Staff commander and at which these Strategic Objectives were enunciated by Karadzic: "The thing that we are doing needs to be guarded as our deepest secret. And what our representatives appearing in the media, at political talks and negotiations, are going to say -- and they need to present our goals in a way that will sound appealing to the ears of those we want to win over to our side without being detrimental to our Serbian people. Our people must know how to read between the lines." Your Honours, in 1994 the accused said to his deputies at an Assembly: "Today we are standing in the same place where we stood at the time of the Lisbon Conference on the eve of the war. The only difference is the number of victims is huge on all three sides. We have ruined cities and somebody is responsible for it, but this is not a question of responsibility now." So who is responsible for the ruined cities, the destroyed mosques and churches, the lost lives, the shattered families, the traumatised survivors? Is it only the camp guards who beat prisoners or watched as others beat them? Is it only the camp commanders who oversaw the crimes being committed on a daily basis? Is it only the municipal leaders like Miroslav Deronjic or Stakic who set up camps, coordinated and supported the military forces, and supervised the ethnic cleansing. Is it only regional leaders like Brdjanin who exhorted Serbs that only a minimum number of non-Serbs could remain and who oversaw the forcible ethnic separation? Is it only the military commanders like Galic and Dragomir Milosevic who conducted campaigns of terror against civilian populations or who oversaw the capture and execution of thousands of Muslims? Is it only the VRS commander of the Main Staff who directed the army's operations and ethnic cleansing in terrorising Sarajevo, in massacring the men and boys of Srebrenica? Or is it also their leader, the supreme commander of the VRS, the president of the SDS, the man who established the institutions, set and implemented the policies, directed his men, and defended their actions? Your Honours, the evidence from the victims and other witnesses, the evidence from internationals, the evidence from official Republika Srpska documents and reports, the evidence from the accused's associates, the evidence from the mouth of the accused himself demonstrates that the answer beyond a reasonable doubt is a resounding yes. Your Honours, this concludes the Prosecution's opening statement. Thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. The accused has absented himself from the trial for consecutive three days, despite having been given several warnings that such attempts to obstruct the proper conduct and progress of the trial would not be tolerated. As I announced last week, the Chamber must now determine the manner in which we will proceed after the Prosecution's opening statement, and we'll hear from the parties on this matter tomorrow afternoon. There will be no evidence heard tomorrow. The purpose of tomorrow's hearing is to give both the accused and the Prosecution the opportunity to make their submissions prior to the Chamber's decision. However, I would like to repeat once again to Mr. Karadzic our previous warnings, and I'll ask the Registry to convey the transcript and the audio recordings of this hearing to him and his assigned legal advisor. Should he maintain his position that he will not attend the trial, we may proceed in his absence and assign counsel to represent him. We advise him to consider this carefully prior to making his oral submissions tomorrow. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
